steps.do: Greet the customer. Ask for every requirement the business checking account must meet: ATM fee rebates, overdraft fees, the highest minimum balance they can keep, the lowest APY, the monthly fee budget and whether it must be waived, the daily mobile deposit amount, debit cashback, and anything else. Customers often state requirements one at a time, so keep asking whether there is anything else until they say nothing else matters. Record each requirement as stated, and recommend nothing until they are done.

steps.do:
Check every business checking product against every stated requirement, using the figures in this job's rules: Beige, Cobalt Blue, Hunter Green, Lime Green, Navy Blue, Sky Blue, True Blue, World Blue. A product that fails any one requirement is out.
- ATM rebates: the product's monthly out-of-network rebate cap must be at least the amount needed. World Blue rebates only foreign ATM operator fees.
- No overdraft fees: the overdraft fee must be $0.00.
- Minimum balance: the product's required ongoing minimum must not exceed what the customer will keep. A fee-waiver threshold is not a minimum.
- APY: the product's APY must be at least min_apy.
- Monthly fee: drop a product on its waiver threshold only if the customer needs the fee waived or avoided. If the customer wants no monthly fee at all and an account that stays free, keep only Navy Blue. Sky Blue's fee becomes $25.00 after its free period.
- Mobile deposits: the daily limit must be at least what the customer needs.
- Debit cashback on general spending: keep only Cobalt Blue. Hunter Green's cashback applies only at certified eco vendors.
- If a product's documents give no figure for a stated requirement, tell the customer and ask whether that product may still be considered.

steps.do:
Use the get_time date to choose ONE account from those that qualify after screen_products and ask_formation.
(a) Exactly one qualifies: choose it.
(b) Date from 10/12/2025 to 10/31/2025 (only the October notice is active): choose Lime Green if it qualifies, otherwise Hunter Green, otherwise go to (e).
(c) Date from 11/13/2025 to 11/30/2025 (only the November notice is active): choose Sky Blue if it qualifies, otherwise Lime Green, otherwise go to (e).
(d) Date from 11/01/2025 to 11/12/2025 (both notices are active):
- If Lime Green qualifies, choose it. October ranks it first and November allows it second, while October's clause (3) bars Sky Blue whenever Lime Green qualifies.
- If Lime Green does not qualify, choose Sky Blue if it qualifies and Hunter Green does not, or Hunter Green if it qualifies and Sky Blue does not.
- If Sky Blue and Hunter Green both qualify, each notice's clause (3) bars the other notice's pick. Tell the customer that both meet every requirement and ask which they prefer.
- If none of the three qualifies, go to (e).
(e) No notice is active, or only accounts outside the notices remain and more than one qualifies: no document ranks them. Explain how each qualifying account meets the customer's requirements and ask which they prefer.

open_questions: account_class format for business checking: doc 003 lists 'Navy Blue, Cobalt Blue, True Blue' without 'Account', while the tool asks for 'the full official account class name' and the product documents name each product '<Name> Account'.
'does not exceed 6 business checking accounts' is ambiguous: it may count existing accounts or the total after opening. The workflow requires that the new account not take the total above 6.

(c) Date 11/13/2025-11/30/2025 (November notice only): Sky Blue if it qualifies, otherwise Lime Green, otherwise another qualifying account. (d) Date 11/01/2025-11/12/2025 (both notices active): Lime Green if it qualifies, because October ranks it first and November allows it second, while October's clause (3) excludes Sky Blue whenever Lime Green qualifies. If Lime Green doesn't qualify: Sky Blue if it qualifies and Hunter Green doesn't; Hunter Green if it qualifies and Sky Blue doesn't. If both Sky Blue and Hunter Green qualify, the two notices conflict: tell the customer both meet their needs and let them choose. (e) No notice active, or several 'other qualifying accounts' remain: no document ranks them, so name each qualifying account and ask the customer to pick. Never mention the promotions to the customer.
